course_title: Risk Management and Information Systems Control
description: This course covers risk identification using ISO 27005; risk assessment with FAIR framework; risk mitigation with NIST SP 800-30; risk quantification using Monte Carlo simulations; risk response planning with ISO 27001; information systems control frameworks like COBIT and COSO ERM; control objectives for IT infrastructure; control implementation using ISO 27002; audit trails and access control mechanisms; incident response using NIST SP 800-61; and risk management in cloud environments using ISO/IEC 27017. It also includes control design for data integrity using SHA-256 hashing; access control models like RBAC and ABAC; and risk evaluation using quantitative models such as the Risk Matrix and Expected Monetary Value (EMV).

clos.text: Define risk management frameworks such as ISO 27005, COBIT, and COSO ERM and their specific applications in information systems.
Describe the FAIR risk assessment framework and its components including threat probability, impact, and risk metrics.
Explain the NIST SP 800-30 risk assessment process and its integration with ISO 27001 controls.
Apply Monte Carlo simulations to quantify risks in IT infrastructure and cloud environments.
Implement control mechanisms like RBAC, access logging, and SHA-256 hashing to ensure data integrity and access control.

topics: Introduction to Risk Management and Information Systems Control
Risk Management Frameworks: ISO 27005, COBIT, COSO ERM
Threat Modeling with STRIDE and DREAD
Quantitative Risk Assessment with FAIR Framework
Monte Carlo Simulations for Risk Analysis
Control Frameworks: COBIT and COSO ERM
Access Control Models: RBAC and ABAC
Final Review of Risk Management Processes
Integration of Risk Management with IT Governance
